prs.title: Prune unused standalone releases after successful installation
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Prune unused standalone releases after successful installation

## What changed

Clean up older standalone releases after verifying the installed command, while holding the install lock. Retain the current and previously selected releases, along with releases used by running Codex processes or bundled helpers.

Record selection history for all standalone installs and preserve it on no-op installs. Only remove validated, installer-owned release directories; skip cleanup when filesystem or process inspection cannot establish that removal is safe. Recheck process usage after moving a release aside and restore it if it is in use.

## Testing

Add installer regression coverage for running helpers, helpers started during cleanup, repeated installs, failed installs, downgrades, and preservation of unowned directories and symlinks.

prs.title: Bucket admitted Guardian request metrics by input size
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Bucket admitted Guardian request metrics by input size

## Why

Guardian request counts grouped by input size should reflect admitted sampling inputs without counting synchronous transport retries more than once.

## What changed

- Add a shared `token_bucket` label to admitted total-input observations in `codex.guardian.context.request_tokens` for synchronous and asynchronous reviews. Use inclusive upper bounds in 20k-token steps through 240k, followed by 256k and overflow buckets.
- Record synchronous request tokens after budget admission, once per sampling step, including the complete input. A fresh step counts again even when its input is identical.
- Preserve asynchronous component histograms for oversized classifications, but omit `token_bucket` so rejected inputs do not contribute to counts grouped by that label.

## Testing

Add coverage for bucket boundaries, synchronous retry deduplication and budget rejection, asynchronous retained-history reuse and reset, and admitted versus oversized classification metrics.

prs.title: Allow plus signs in metric tags
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Allow plus signs in metric tags

## Why

App versions containing build metadata use `+`, which metric tag validation previously rejected.

## What changed

Accept `+` in metric tag keys and values so these versions can be included in the `app.version` session tag.

## Testing

Extend the session metric tag test to cover a version with build metadata, verifying that its value and tag ordering are preserved.

prs.title: Record Guardian sampling retries, attempts, and delivery outcomes
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Record Guardian sampling retries, attempts, and delivery outcomes

## What changed

- Add sampling retry counters that distinguish transport retries from authentication recovery, with failure reasons.
- Record attempt counts and final outcomes for successful, failed, cancelled, and superseded sampling requests.
- Carry retained-score telemetry until the consumer accepts or discards the score, so queued scores that expire are recorded as superseded and accepted early scores remain successful even if response draining fails.

## Testing

Add metric assertions for transient recovery, retry exhaustion, authentication recovery, cancellation, supersession, and retained-score acceptance or discard, including expiry while a score is queued.

prs.title: Add Guardian review routing and cached score metrics
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add Guardian review routing and cached score metrics

## What changed

- Count adaptive reviews and record synchronous review routes as `async_fallback` or `required_sync`, with the review reason in snake case.
- Record cached score readiness and score age in milliseconds, measured from input sampling time and including inference time.

## Testing

Extend approval tests to assert fallback routing, adaptive review counts, score readiness, and sampled score age.

prs.title: Batch thread history materialization into SQLite
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Batch thread history materialization into SQLite

## Why

History catch-up collected the entire durable rollout prefix before applying it in one SQLite transaction. Large rollouts therefore required buffering all projection steps and committing them together.

## What changed

Stream projection batches through a bounded queue and commit each batch with its checkpoint. Flush between complete records after reaching 1 MiB of source data or 256 projection steps, keeping ordinal gaps with their following records and allowing oversized records to remain intact.

Wait for batches before opening SQLite transactions so an idle reader does not hold the writer. Preserve committed progress across later failures or cancellation, allowing retries to resume from the last checkpoint.

## Testing

Add coverage for reader and writer failures under backpressure, atomic batch rollback, retries without replaying committed records, and unrelated writes while projection is paused. Verify that producer disconnection and consumer cancellation retain committed progress.

prs.title: Preserve rollout access metadata across compression and restoration
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve rollout access metadata across compression and restoration

## Why

Replacing rollout files can lose Unix ownership or macOS ACLs, changing who can read or append to a transcript. An ACL can also permit appending while denying explicit timestamp updates.

## What changed

- Preserve Unix ownership, permissions, modification times, and macOS ACLs before publishing compressed or restored rollouts, and verify the replacement can be reopened.
- Abort replacement on metadata failures, reject macOS delete-deny ACLs to keep temporary files removable, and detect Unix access metadata changes through `ctime` checks.
- Use managed restoration temporary files whose names avoid stale `*.tmp` cleanup.
- Allow appending when refreshing the rollout's modification time returns `PermissionDenied`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for macOS ACL preservation, inherited ACL removal, deletion-protected rollouts, append access despite denied timestamp changes, Unix group preservation, and restoration temporary files surviving stale-file cleanup.

prs.title: Unload idle ephemeral composer prediction threads without delay
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Unload idle ephemeral composer prediction threads without delay

## What changed

Set the app server's unload delay to zero for ephemeral threads whose `thread_source` is `composer_predictions`, excluding subagent sessions. These threads unload once they are idle and have no subscribers, while active turns continue to completion.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage to check immediate unloading after an active prediction turn finishes and after unsubscribing from a fork that inherits the prediction configuration. Verify that persistent threads and ephemeral threads without the prediction source retain the configured delay.

prs.title: Share dynamic tool specifications across turn snapshots
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Share dynamic tool specifications across turn snapshots

## What changed

Store dynamic tool specifications in an `Arc<[DynamicToolSpec]>` so session configuration and turn snapshots share the list fixed at thread startup instead of copying it on each clone.

Keep the `dynamic_tools()` accessor returning a `Vec<DynamicToolSpec>`, but copy the specifications after releasing the session state lock.

prs.title: Stop memory dual-write when v2 is selected
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Stop memory dual-write when v2 is selected

## Why

Dual-write prepares v2 memories while v1 is selected. Once v2 is selected, running the v1 pipeline is no longer needed.

## What changed

Run both memory pipelines only when `memories.dual_write` is enabled and `memories.version` selects v1. Run only v2 when it is selected, even if dual-write remains enabled. Update the configuration documentation and schema to describe this behavior.

## Testing

Extend the startup test to cover both selected versions, checking model request counts, versioned extraction and consolidation state, and the absence of v1 rollout summaries when v2 is selected.

prs.title: Start dormant MCP servers for hook calls
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Start dormant MCP servers for hook calls

## Why

MCP tool hooks need to invoke model-hidden tools even when a subagent's cached server has not started. Their timeout must also cover server startup.

## What changed

- Let cached servers with allowed model-hidden tools remain dormant until called.
- Wait for the selected server when executing an MCP hook, leaving unrelated cached servers dormant, and apply the hook timeout to the entire operation.
- Capture tool namespace attribution after startup and retain it only while catalog revisions remain unchanged.
- Validate the server, environment, and tool filter before starting a server or capturing attribution.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for cached subagent hooks under both startup readiness modes, startup timeouts without context injection, and namespace attribution for hook and token-budget context while keeping tools hidden from the model. Verify that a direct call starts a cached server whose tools are hidden from model exposure.

prs.title: Avoid cloning the full catalog for model metadata lookups
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Avoid cloning the full catalog for model metadata lookups

## Why

`get_model_info` clones the entire model catalog before selecting metadata for a single model.

## What changed

Look up metadata directly in the active catalog for both remote and static model managers. Share catalog selection across remote catalog accessors and metadata lookup, preserving auth identity checks, API-key discovery policy, provider matching rules, and configuration overrides.

## Testing

Extend coverage for custom catalog configuration overrides, metadata fallback after disabling API-key discovery, and fallback after an auth identity change.

prs.title: Honor per-thread unload delays in app-server
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Honor per-thread unload delays in app-server

## Why

Thread unload timing used the server-wide delay, ignoring per-thread configuration overrides. Clients need to control how long individual idle, unsubscribed threads remain loaded.

## What changed

- Resolve unload timing from each loaded thread's `thread_unload_delay_secs` configuration. Setting it to `0` allows immediate unloading once the thread has no subscribers or activity.
- Allow this runtime retention override in `experimentalPredictionMode` forks while continuing to reject other configuration overrides. Reject negative values and delays too large to schedule.
- Replace the source-specific immediate-unload behavior with explicit configuration.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for per-thread delays, unloading after active turns finish, fork overrides, and invalid prediction-fork delays. Verify that immediate unloading preserves persistent history and that cold resumes and ordinary nested forks use their default delay instead of retaining the previous runtime's override.

prs.title: Stabilize daemon reconnect and Rosetta package startup tests
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Stabilize daemon reconnect and Rosetta package startup tests

## Why

A replacement daemon PID can appear before the TUI observes the disconnect, allowing stale UI content to make the startup test advance too early. Cold Rosetta translation can also consume the startup deadlines for freshly extracted Intel macOS packages on Apple Silicon.

## What changed

- Wait for the reconnect transcript clear before sending `/status` in the daemon startup test.
- Warm both packaged CLI and app-server entrypoints with `--help` when testing `x86_64-apple-darwin` packages on `arm64` hosts. Give each warmup 180 seconds and fail fixture setup if either entrypoint cannot run.

prs.title: Fall back when macOS rejects high stdio descriptors
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fall back when macOS rejects high stdio descriptors

## Why

On macOS, spawn file actions reject valid descriptors at or above `OPEN_MAX` even when `RLIMIT_NOFILE` permits them. This can prevent child processes from starting when their stdio descriptors exceed that limit.

## What changed

Use the compatibility backend when `posix_spawn_file_actions_adddup2` returns `EBADF` for stdio setup and `SpawnFallback::Compatible` is enabled. Preserve the error for `SpawnFallback::ReturnError`.

## Testing

Add a macOS regression test that forces high stdio descriptors and checks strict-mode errors, fallback stdio and exit status, process groups, and descriptor isolation without changing the parent's descriptor.

prs.title: Avoid cloning events in the app-server thread listener
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Avoid cloning events in the app-server thread listener

Record whether an event is `ShutdownComplete` before moving it into
`apply_bespoke_event_handling`, preserving shutdown drain notification without
cloning the event.

prs.title: Track MCP enterprise auth cancellation across config reloads
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Track MCP enterprise auth cancellation across config reloads

## Why

Configuration loading can finish before a pending startup is visible to the thread manager. Reloads need a cancellation scope that also covers these configuration snapshots.

## What changed

- Capture an enterprise managed authentication (EMA) cancellation token before loading configuration and carry it through config layers, role overrides, runtime refreshes, and `McpConfig`.
- Cancel the previous scope on MCP or user configuration reloads and cloud config loader changes, then create a fresh scope for subsequent loads.
- Cancel the session's token when enterprise MCP authentication is disabled or a refresh leaves it unavailable.

## Testing

Extend the MCP reload test to verify that existing thread and pending startup tokens are cancelled while a fresh startup receives an uncancelled token.

prs.title: Recheck EMA request authority at HTTP boundaries
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Recheck EMA request authority at HTTP boundaries

## Why

Authorization can change during token renewal before a revocation watcher runs. Requests must check that their authority is still current before dispatch.

## What changed

- Let `EmaRequestAuthority` accept a cancellation token and a synchronous authority check, revoking itself when the check fails.
- Recheck authority after authentication and after receiving HTTP responses for both regular and streaming requests.
- Add `CloudConfigBundleBinding::invalidated()` to wait until a captured policy binding is no longer current.

## Testing

Update tests to cover ownership changing during token renewal without explicit revocation, preventing HTTP dispatch, and parent-token cancellation ending an existing response stream.

prs.title: Keep only the latest adjacent reasoning effort update in requests
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Keep only the latest adjacent reasoning effort update in requests

## Why

Turn recovery and retries after a server overload can leave consecutive reasoning effort updates in history when settings change without an intervening message. Requests should use the latest update in each consecutive run.

## What changed

Coalesce adjacent `configuration_update` items when building Responses requests with reasoning effort overrides enabled, retaining the latest update. Preserve saved history and updates separated by other input items.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for recovery with unchanged or changed effort, retries after a server overload, and WebSocket continuation and replay after coalescing. Verify that requests retain the latest adjacent update while saved history keeps all updates.

prs.title: Encapsulate Responses API proxy authentication
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Encapsulate Responses API proxy authentication

## What changed

Introduce a shared `Auth` abstraction that supplies sensitive authorization headers and the client's redirect policy. Preserve the existing static API key allocation and default redirect behavior, and return an empty `502` response if header acquisition fails.

Unify the stdin authentication entry point around platform-specific `read_from_stdin` helpers.

## Testing

Add a test verifying that both compact and pretty `Debug` output redact API keys.

prs.title: Add GitHub Actions OIDC token acquisition to the responses API proxy
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add GitHub Actions OIDC token acquisition to the responses API proxy

## What changed

Add a `GithubOidc` implementation of `SubjectTokenSource` that requests a fresh token using a bearer credential read from stdin. Validate HTTPS request URLs and replace the audience query parameter while preserving other parameters. CLI integration is not included.

Add a token HTTP client that disables redirects and request logging, applies timeouts, and bounds response bodies. Keep token response buffers in zeroizing storage and exclude credentials, request URLs, and response bodies from errors.

Generalize the locked stdin credential reader for bounded OIDC bearer tokens while preserving API key validation.

## Testing

Add tests for fresh token acquisition, short reads, credential size limits, injection rejection, redirect refusal, and credential-safe errors and logs. Extend API key tests to retain the stricter character restrictions.

prs.title: Add renewable federated auth primitives to the Responses API proxy
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add renewable federated auth primitives to the Responses API proxy

## What changed

Add a federated `Auth` variant that exchanges JWT subject tokens for OpenAI access tokens using identity provider and service account IDs. Serialize concurrent exchanges, cache credentials, and renew proactively with a fresh subject token.

Validate token types, bearer credentials, payload sizes, and lifetimes. Bound caching by both relative and absolute expiry, discard cached credentials before renewal, and disable redirects for federated requests. Keep credential buffers zeroizing and diagnostics free of secrets.

## Testing

Add HTTP fixture tests for concurrent cache reuse, renewal with fresh subjects, expiry across host suspension, failed renewal, oversized payloads, invalid subjects, and unsupported or missing issued token types.

prs.title: Refresh rejected proxy credentials and back off failed renewals
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Refresh rejected proxy credentials and back off failed renewals

## Why

The Responses API proxy could reuse a federated credential after an upstream `401`, and concurrent requests could each retry a failed token exchange.

## What changed

- Invalidate the rejected credential so the next request obtains a fresh token. Forward the `401` without replaying the request or waiting for an ongoing renewal; leave credentials intact on `403`.
- Track rejection per token issuance so a late `401` cannot invalidate a newer credential.
- Back off failed exchanges exponentially from 1 to 30 seconds, starting when the exchange fails. Reject requests during backoff without reusing the old token, and reset the delay after a successful exchange.

## Testing

Add tests for response forwarding without replay, late and concurrent rejections, shared renewal failures, backoff timing and reset, and credential-safe renewal errors without following redirects.

prs.title: Add one-shot app-server startup configuration discovery
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add one-shot app-server startup configuration discovery

## What changed

Add `codex app-server --print-startup-config` to validate local and cloud-backed configuration and emit the app-server version and configuration requirements as JSON without initializing environments, thread storage, or plugins. Configuration failures produce structured JSON errors and a nonzero exit status.

Support `--startup-sign-out` to remove account credentials and reload signed-out requirements, including recovery when cloud policy is unavailable. Reject sign-out for host-owned external authentication. Accept `--startup-client-info` to identify configuration and authentication requests.

Reuse configuration loading and account cleanup logic between startup discovery and the running app server.

## Testing

Add CLI integration coverage for configuration validation, project login restrictions, managed cloud requirements and failures, sign-out recovery, external authentication protection, and independence from locked or invalid history databases.

prs.title: Reconcile V2 executor plugins with cloud catalogs
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Reconcile V2 executor plugins with cloud catalogs

## What changed

- Use V2 discovery inventories for plugin MCP contributions when supplied, including empty or failed inventories; retain legacy discovery when no V2 snapshot is supplied.
- Merge plugins by canonical identity, using cloud metadata and enablement for remote plugins and attaching executor installations only when versions match. Preserve configured executor-local plugins and executor enablement when cloud data is unavailable.
- Keep installation order stable across refreshes and run merged MCP declarations on the first retained executor installation while preserving attribution for the others.
- Carry local and remote identities through selected-plugin snapshots, skill attribution, and active-plugin telemetry. Track disabled plugin IDs alongside disabled roots.
- Preserve a complete cloud catalog when a partial refresh arrives, and cap tool-description plugin attribution at 1,024 bytes while retaining all plugin associations.

## Testing

Add coverage for catalog parsing and reconciliation, enablement and discovery-mode selection, installation refresh ordering, executor-specific MCP normalization, selected-plugin snapshots, and bounded UTF-8 attribution text.

prs.title: Stop the closest remote SHA search at zero distance
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Stop the closest remote SHA search at zero distance

Return immediately from `find_closest_sha` when a remote-backed branch has
zero distance from `HEAD`, avoiding Git commands for the remaining candidates
once the minimum possible distance is found.

prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Check daemon feature overrides and prompt for mismatch recovery

## Why

A fixed feature allowlist excluded other boolean feature overrides from daemon use. Feature mismatches could also silently fall back to embedded mode, while automatic startup could persist enabled overrides without confirmation.

## What changed

- Allow boolean feature overrides without a fixed allowlist and compare explicit overrides with the daemon's reported settings. Ignore removed features, treat unreported features as disabled, and include only mismatches in restart settings.
- Preserve saved daemon settings during automatic startup. Prompt on feature mismatches even when embedded fallback is allowed, letting users run without the daemon, confirm a managed-daemon restart, or cancel.
- Detect managed daemons during recovery, mark available restarts as recommended, and limit the displayed feature list to three entries plus a remaining count.

## Testing

Update compatibility tests for mixed overrides, removed and unreported features, unreachable daemons, and required versus optional attachment. Update recovery snapshots and the TUI integration test to exercise explicit embedded-mode selection.

prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix in-process app-server shutdown with full queues

## Why

When unread events block notification delivery and the client request queue is full, shutdown can hang waiting to enqueue its shutdown message before reaching its timeouts.

## What changed

Drop the event receiver at the start of `InProcessClientHandle::shutdown` to unblock notification delivery before waiting for space in the request queue.

## Testing

Add a regression test that fills both queues with real requests and notifications, then verifies shutdown completes within the configured timeout budget.

Fix TUI permission selection and session state handling
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix TUI permission selection and session state handling

## Why

Queued prompts can resume before a pending permissions menu opens, and local
`/permissions` commands can bypass guards for outstanding permission changes.
Attaching to a different project can also retain model access information from
the launch directory.

## What changed

- Route `/permissions` through app permission guards and hold queued prompts
  while the menu is pending. Settle the hold when opening is rejected, discovery
  is invalidated, or a covering request is resolved.
- Apply the custom permission profile selection check beyond embedded servers.
- Refresh API-key model access when the first attached session changes the
  working directory, including with an embedded server. Propagate the widget's
  model catalog to the app and server even when the model response matches the
  widget's already-updated catalog.
- Skip sessions reported as `thread not loaded` during name lookup for all
  server types instead of falling back to unverified list metadata.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for permission guards, queued prompts across successive
permission menus, invalidated and covered menus, model catalog propagation,
project changes on initial attachment, and name lookup across server pages with
unreadable entries.
